title: Add reusable zero-allocation animation pose buffer
description:
## Summary
Introduce a reusable indexed mutable pose buffer for high-frequency animation frames so animation does not allocate a complete immutable pose snapshot or vector array on every tick.

## Scope
- Hold indexed position and rotation data for one creature skeleton.
- Validate skeleton identity, count, finite data, and compatibility at initialization and application boundaries.
- Make rest-pose reset and copy semantics explicit.
- Keep immutable pose snapshots for interchange and diagnostics.
- Do not add clip playback, locomotion, blending policy, Animator/Avatar integration, or speculative pooling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One reusable buffer supports indexed position and rotation updates for a compatible skeleton.
- Reuse performs no managed allocations after warmup in the focused runtime harness.
- Rest-pose reset, incompatible skeleton rejection, malformed lengths, and non-finite values have focused tests.
- Applying the buffer does not regenerate geometry, recalculate weights, resolve semantic IDs, or rebuild the renderer.
- TSK-0134 remains the owner of authoritative Unity PlayMode and profiler performance evidence.

## Validation
Run whole-project .NET compilation before focused runtime tests. Record exact allocation results. Unity PlayMode and profiler evidence are required for the performance gate and must not be claimed from source inspection.

## Findings
The animation roadmap and independent review confirm that immutable PosedSkeleton construction and caller-side string-to-index preparation are unsuitable as the per-frame mechanism. The prior record was created with the colliding key TSK-0189. This record replaces that duplicate with a unique MemorySmith key and coordinates with TSK-0134 rather than duplicating its benchmark ownership.

## Blockers
Unity execution is unavailable during this reconciliation. The task remains Backlog until implementation and focused tests exist.

## Next Step
Define the buffer contract after TSK-0190 and prove runtime reuse before any renderer integration.
